citation: Sarabdjitsingh, R. A., Loi, M., Joëls, M., Dijkhuizen, R. M., & van der Toorn, A. (2017). Early life stress-induced alterations in rat brain structures measured with high resolution MRI. PLOS ONE, 12(9), e0185061. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0185061
caption: Table 1. Volumes of the different ROIs based on high-resolution anatomical MRI. N = 10 rats per group. Data represents mean ± SEM in μl and was analyzed using 2-way ANOVA with MD and mifepristone treatment as main factors. Statistical significance based on p-values for the main effect is presented in the last three columns: * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, ns = not significant.
note: Maternal deprivation for 24 h at P3. Four experimental arms retained; primary deprivation contrast is MD vs noMD within vehicle. PFC overlaps its OFC, mPFC and insular subdivisions; never sum or fit parent and children together. Table n=10 per group retained as nominal; model degrees of freedom vary. 1 μl = 1 mm3.
